Consult Summary:
- 49-year-old woman with 2-week progressive left upper extremity paresthesia, numbness and mild weakness with intermittent tingling in the 2nd–4th digits (palmar surface) and a brief transient left visual field loss; urgent neurology referral arranged for further investigation.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Progressive numbness, tingling and subjective weakness of the left arm for approximately two weeks.
  - Intermittent tingling in fingertips and numbness from elbow to hand; currently tingling in some fingers.
  - Transient loss of part of the visual field in the left eye for ~20 minutes several weeks ago (resolved).
  - Occasional shoulder discomfort with activity (boxing); initially typed "jaw pain" on intake but patient clarified jaw pain is not primary.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began ~2 weeks ago after starting a boxing class a few weeks earlier.
  - Initially mild tingling, progressively worsened to numbness and some weakness.
  - Attempted self-treatment with massage and warm baths without improvement.
  - Took ibuprofen intermittently for muscle/knuckle soreness.
  - Transient visual symptom occurred a few weeks ago and lasted about 20 minutes, then resolved.
  - Recent febrile/viral illness about 1 month ago with ~2 weeks of illness.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Symptoms may be associated with boxing activity; worsened over time.
  - Massage and warm baths did not relieve numbness.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Left arm: numbness, tingling (palmar 2nd–4th digits), subjective weakness, occasional difficulty with fine motor tasks (piano).
  - Vision: brief transient left visual field loss lasting ~20 minutes, resolved.
  - No reported seizures, loss of consciousness, vomiting, or new headaches beyond occasional fatigue/tension-type headaches.
  - Gait and lower extremity function reported as normal.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No ongoing visual loss at time of consult.
  - No reported limb weakness on the right or leg weakness.
  - No reported fevers at time of consult.
  - No reported use of glasses/contacts.
  - No documentation of focal neurological exam findings in the visit.

Past Medical History:
- Generally healthy by patient report.
- Recent viral/flu-like illness approximately 1 month prior, symptomatic for ~2 weeks.
- No chronic medical conditions explicitly reported by patient.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen — dose/route/frequency not documented (used intermittently for muscle/knuckle soreness).
- Vitamin D — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Melatonin — dose/route/frequency not documented (used intermittently for sleep).
- Iron supplements recommended by GP but largely not taken (patient reports forgetting; dose/route/frequency not documented).
Allergies:
- Not documented.

Social History:
- Exercises regularly; recently started a boxing class a few weeks ago.
- Alcohol: recent episode of heavy alcohol consumption associated with an illness; no regular alcohol use pattern documented.
- Smoking/tobacco use: not documented.
- Illicit drug use: not documented.
- Employment/lifestyle: works long hours; reports fatigue related to work and exercise.
- No other social determinants or financial factors mentioned.

Family History:
- Father: hypothyroidism and "some autoimmune stuff" (details not specified).
- Mother: type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
- No other neurological conditions in family reported.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No formal physical examination findings documented in the transcript.

Investigations:
- No imaging or laboratory results available.
- Plan discussed for urgent neurology referral and brain scan (type of scan not specified).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left upper extremity numbness, tingling (palmar 2nd–4th digits) and subjective weakness
  - Assessment: Progressive focal sensory symptoms with motor difficulty (patient-reported); differential discussed includes orthopaedic/entrapment injury related to boxing and central causes (physician raised possibility of multiple sclerosis).
  - Plan:
    - Urgent neurology referral arranged.
    - Recommend neuroimaging ("brain scan") and further neurological workup by neurology.
    - No steroid or other treatment started pending diagnostic clarification.
    - Safety advice: attend emergency department if symptoms progress (new/worsening weakness including legs), development of severe headache, vomiting, seizures, or worsening visual symptoms.
- Issue 2: Transient left visual field loss (single episode, ~20 minutes, resolved)
  - Assessment: Concerning transient visual disturbance; may be related to central nervous system process per clinician.
  - Plan:
    - Include visual symptom in urgent neurology referral and imaging workup.
    - No acute ophthalmology referral documented; vision stable at time of consult.
- Issue 3: Recent viral illness (1 month prior)
  - Assessment: Recent febrile/flu-like illness may be temporally related to current symptoms but not confirmed.
  - Plan:
    - Document history for neurology assessment; no specific treatment directed at postinfectious causes during this consult.
- General plan items:
  - Clinician to initiate urgent neurology referral and arrange appropriate imaging/investigations.
  - Do not start steroids or other disease-specific therapies until diagnosis is confirmed.
  - Patient instructed to go to A&E for red-flag deterioration (progressive weakness, severe headache, vomiting, seizures, worsening vision).

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs documented.
  - No focused neurological or general physical examination findings recorded.
  - No documented ophthalmologic exam findings.
  - No imaging or laboratory test results available.
  - Medication doses, routes and frequencies not documented.
  - Allergies, smoking status, and substance use not documented.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Initial presenting problem on intake included "jaw pain" but patient later clarified this was not the main issue.
  - Conflicting statements regarding neck pain: patient alternately indicated "Yes, absolutely" and "No, not, no, nothing" when asked; conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally understandable; occasional overlapping speech and brief interruptions but overall adequate for clinical summary.
